I'll need to:\n1. Create a semaphore with max_concurrent\n2. Create a task for each input callable\n3. Use the semaphore to limit concurrency\n4. Handle interruption gracefully\n\nA good approach is to wrap each task with the semaphore, and then gather all tasks with return_exceptions=True so that interruptions don't immediately cancel everything.\n\nHere's my approach:\n```python\nimport asyncio\nfrom typing import Callable, Awaitable\n\nasync def run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None:\n    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)\n    \n    async def bounded_task(task):\n        async with semaphore:\n            await task()\n    \n    # Create all tasks\n    all_tasks = [asyncio.create_task(bounded_task(task())) for task in tasks]\n    \n    # Wait for all tasks with exception handling\n    try:\n        await asyncio.gather(*all_tasks)\n    except KeyboardInterrupt:\n        # Allow tasks to continue running their cleanup code\n        # Cancel all tasks but wait for them\n        for task in all_tasks:\n            task.cancel()\n        # Wait for all tasks to finish\n        await asyncio.gather(*all_tasks, return_exceptions=True)\n        raise\n```\n\nThere's a subtlety here since `task()` produces the awaitable itself, so `bounded_task` should accept the callable and call it inside, not the already-created coroutine. I need to fix this so semaphore acquisition happens before invoking the callable, avoiding creating unbounded coroutines upfront.\n\n```python\nasync def run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None:\n    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)\n    \n    async def bounded_task(task_callable):\n        async with semaphore:\n            await task_callable()\n    \n    all_tasks = [asyncio.create_task(bounded_task(task)) for task in tasks]\n    \n    try:\n        await asyncio.gather(*all_tasks)\n    except KeyboardInterrupt:\n        for task in all_tasks:\n            task.cancel()\n        await asyncio.gather(*all_tasks, return_exceptions=True)\n        raise\n```\n\nThis limits concurrency correctly via the semaphore while still creating all task objects upfront, and cleans up properly on interrupt.\n\nCancelling a task raises `CancelledError` inside it, so any try/finally cleanup the user has written will still execute.
